decision_conditions: Temporary Time LimitA.	This permission shall be for a limited period of five years from the date of this decision notice.  B.	No later than six months prior to the expiration date of this time limited permission, a future use strategy of the land shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority setting out the reasons for the continued need of the security hut and hoarding, or an alternative strategy for the use of the land. The hereby approved security hut and hoarding shall then be removed in their entirety on or before the expiry of this permission unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To enable the Local Planning Authority to review the suitability of the development in light of circumstances prevailing at the end of the above period, and in the interests of the character and appearance of the area and the amenity of surrounding residential occupiers.

Approved PlansThe development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: T291100, T291101, T291102, T298200, T220200, T298400, T218100, T210200Design and Access statement, dated 16/12/2025, P01Ecology Technical Note, prepared by Crossland Ecology Ltd, dated 22.12.25Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

No development shall take place, including any works of demolition, until a Construction Method Statement (CMS), including a Demolition and Construction Traffic Management Plan, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CMS shall include, but not be limited to, the following measures:Site Logistics and Access:a) A site set-up plan during the works.Details of any temporary construction access to the site, including measures for removal following completion of construction works.Parking of vehicles for site operatives and visitors.Loading and unloading of plant and materials.Storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development, clear of the highway.A map showing the routing of demolition and construction vehicles to and from the site.b) Highway and Transport Safeguards:A photographic condition survey of public carriageways, verges and footways in the vicinity of the site.Details of access arrangements to the site.Wheel cleaning methodology and facilities to ensure mud and debris are not deposited on the public highway.c) Site Management:Erection and maintenance of security hoarding, including any decorative displays and/or facilities for public viewing, where appropriate.Measures to control the emission of dust, dirt, noise, vibration, odour, surface water runoff, and pests/vermin during demolition and construction.d) Environmental Safeguards:A scheme for recycling and/or disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works.Measures to prevent pollution from surface water runoff during construction.e) Construction Operations:A detailed method statement and programme for the demolition and construction works.Hours of deliveries and preferred haulage routes.Delivery, demolition and construction working hours. Demolition or construction works shall only take place between 08:00 and 18:00 on Mondays to Fridays and between 08:00 and 13:00 on Saturdays, and shall not take place at any time on Sundays or Bank or Public Holidays.f) Contact Information:Contact details for the responsible person (site manager/office) who can be contacted in the event of any issue.The approved CMS shall be adhered to and implemented throughout the demolition and construction period in accordance with the approved details, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that the impact of the development on the surrounding transport network, residential amenity, and environment is appropriately assessed and mitigated, in accordance with Policy DMD48 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014) and Policy T7 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to the commencement of the installation of the site hut and hoarding, and prior to the demolition hereby approved a scheme for the protection of the retained trees, in accordance with BS 5837:2012, including a tree protection plan (TPP) and an arboricultural method statement (AMS) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Specific issues to be dealt with in the TPP and AMS:a) methods of demolition within the root protection area (RPA as defined in BS 5837: 2012) of theretained trees;b) methodology of demolition to ensure the trunks and the crowns of the retained trees are notdamaged as well as the roots;c) a specification for protective fencing to safeguard trees during both demolition and constructionphases and a plan indicating the alignment of the protective fencing;d) a specification for scaffolding and ground protection within tree protection zones;The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: To Ensure trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality.
The proposed security hut shall only be used as a security hut for the security and management of the site and for no other purpose.Reason: To prevent unauthorised use and safeguard amenity.

No advertisements, signage or promotional material shall be displayed on the site hoarding unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority or where consent is granted under the Town and Country Planning (Control of Advertisements) (England) Regulations 2007.Reason: To safeguard visual amenity and ensure compliance with advertisement control.
